messages.author: d067fbd7b8a8f3fe
messages.subject: Fatal error with Scantwo
parts:
Hi Dr Karl

I'm trying to run scantwo on 1116 markers with permutation = 100 but the software just crashes. 

DArT1116P2a <- calc.genoprob(DArT1116P2a, step = 0, err = 0.001)
out2.hk <- scantwo(DArT1116P2a, pheno.col = 2:16, method = "hk", verbose = FALSE)
summary(out2.hk, thresholds = c(3.5,2,1.5,2,1.1))
max(out2.hk)

operm2.hk <- scantwo(DArT1116P2a, pheno.col = 2:16, method = "hk", n.perm = 100)


What could be the problem?


Thank you in advance

Celesta

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Fatal error with Scantwo

permutations at a time.

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Fatal error with Scantwo
parts:
Since you’re using method=“hk”, I would recommend trying scantwopermhk(), which reorganizes some of the calculations to try to save memory. 

I don’t think memory.limit() does anything useful. You need to either work with a machine with more RAM, or break things down into smaller pieces. 

karl

Dear Dr Karl

I am working on 20 traits, is it possible to run scantwopermhk() on all the traits at the same time?

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Fatal error with Scantwo
parts:
On Wednesday, April 24, 2019 at 8:43:41 AM UTC-5, Celesta Lephuthing wrote:
Dr Karl

I do not quite understand what you mean by "loop over multiple traits" as I am new in the qtl and command world. May you please elaborate?

You need to call the function repeatedly, once for each trait. One way to do that would be with a for() loop, something like this:

    phe_index <- 2:21
    operm2 <- vector("list", length(phe_index))
    for(i in seq_along(phe_index)) {
        operm2[[i]] <- scantwopermhk(SNP1, chr = 1:20, pheno.col = phe_index[i], n.perm = 1000,

batchsize = 1000, verbose = TRUE, assumeCondIndep = TRUE)
    }
karl
